statement: Distributed continuity inherits F1 continuity semantics and does not redefine them.
Continuity is a property of the execution path, not merely the endpoint.
Economic endpoint equivalence does not imply continuity preservation.
Atomic completion does not imply continuity preservation.
Settlement finality does not imply continuity preservation.
Reconciliation does not imply continuity preservation.
Compensation does not imply continuity preservation.
Reversal does not imply continuity preservation.
Canonical branch selection does not imply continuity preservation.
Functional recovery does not imply continuity preservation.
Reconstructed continuity is distinct from preserved continuity.
Local continuity does not imply cross-domain continuity.
A historical break remains historically classified even after later recovery.
Current preserved state does not imply historically uninterrupted continuity.
Indeterminate continuity cannot be promoted to preserved.
